subject: math
title: Divide Fractions by Fractions
seo_title: Grade 6 Dividing Fractions by Fractions Worksheets: Reciprocals, Keep-Change-Flip, Mixed Numbers and Word Problems
standard_text: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions, and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem. For example, create a story context for (2/3) ÷ (3/4) and use a visual fraction model to show the quotient; use the relationship between multiplication and division to explain that (2/3) ÷ (3/4) = 8/9 because 3/4 of 8/9 is 2/3. (In general, (a/b) ÷ (c/d) = ad/bc.) How much chocolate will each person get if 3 people share 1/2 lb of chocolate equally? How many 3/4-cup servings are in 2/3 of a cup of yogurt? How wide is a rectangular strip of land with length 3/4 mi and area 1/2 square mi?
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 worksheets on dividing fractions by fractions: use fraction bars to find how many groups fit, multiply by the reciprocal, divide mixed numbers and whole numbers, check with multiplication, and solve serving, sharing and area word problems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: To divide by a fraction, multiply by its reciprocal: 2/3 ÷ 3/4 = 2/3 × 4/3 = 8/9.
key_sub: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, flip the second. Change mixed numbers to fractions first. Check: 3/4 × 8/9 = 2/3.
body_html:
The big idea: how many groups?

34 ÷ 18 asks: how many groups of 18 fit in 34? Write both fractions with the same denominator and count.

Sometimes only part of a group fits. Then the answer is a fraction or a mixed number.

The rule: multiply by the reciprocal

The reciprocal of a fraction is the fraction flipped: the reciprocal of 34 is 43. A number times its reciprocal is 1.

To divide, keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second fraction. In general, ab ÷ cd = adbc.

Example 1

23 ÷ 34 = ?

Keep 23, change ÷ to ×, flip 34: 23 × 43 = 89. Check: 34 × 89 = 2436 = 23.

Answer: 89

Example 2

2 12 ÷ 34 = ?

Write 2 12 as 52. Then 52 × 43 = 206 = 3 13.

Answer: 3 13

Example 3

3 people share 12 pound of chocolate equally. How much does each person get?

12 ÷ 3 = 12 × 13 = 16. Check: 16 × 3 = 36 = 12.

Answer: 16 pound

Check with multiplication

Multiply the answer by the divisor. You should get the number you started with.

DivisionCheck
23 ÷ 34 = 8934 × 89 = 23
4 ÷ 23 = 623 × 6 = 4

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
56 ÷ 23 = 65 × 23 (flipped the first fraction)Flip only the divisor: 56 × 32 = 1 14
56 ÷ 23 = 1018 (multiplied without flipping)Flip the second fraction before you multiply.
2 12 ÷ 34 = 2 23 (divided only the fraction part)Change mixed numbers to fractions first: 52 × 43 = 3 13
1 ÷ 23 = 1 13 (leftover written as part of a whole)The leftover 13 is half of a 23 group, so the answer is 1 12

faq.q: How do you divide a fraction by a fraction?
faq.a: Keep the first fraction, change ÷ to ×, and flip the second fraction, then multiply. For example, 2/3 ÷ 3/4 = 2/3 × 4/3 = 8/9.

faq.q: Why do you flip the second fraction when dividing?
faq.a: Dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal. You can check it: 3/4 × 8/9 = 2/3, so 2/3 ÷ 3/4 really is 8/9.

faq.q: How do you divide mixed numbers?
faq.a: Change each mixed number to a fraction first, then multiply by the reciprocal of the divisor. 2 1/2 ÷ 3/4 = 5/2 × 4/3 = 10/3 = 3 1/3.

faq.q: What grade learns dividing fractions by fractions?
faq.a: Grade 6, in Common Core standard 6.NS.A.1. In Grade 5, students divide only unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.

sets.title: How many groups? Use a fraction bar

items.q:
The bar shows 34. How many groups of 18 are in 34?
34 ÷ 18 = ?
items.e: Use eighths: 34 = 68. Each group is 1 eighth. 6 eighths make 6 ÷ 1 = 6 groups. So 34 ÷ 18 = 6. Check: 6 × 18 = 34.

items.q:
The bar shows 2. How many groups of 23 are in 2?
2 ÷ 23 = ?
items.e: Use thirds: 2 = 63. Each group is 2 thirds. 6 thirds make 6 ÷ 2 = 3 groups. So 2 ÷ 23 = 3. Check: 3 × 23 = 2.

items.q:
The bar shows 34. How many groups of 38 are in 34?
34 ÷ 38 = ?
items.e: Use eighths: 34 = 68. Each group is 3 eighths. 6 eighths make 6 ÷ 3 = 2 groups. So 34 ÷ 38 = 2. Check: 2 × 38 = 34.

items.q:
The bar shows 56. How many groups of 112 are in 56?
56 ÷ 112 = ?
items.e: Use twelfths: 56 = 1012. Each group is 1 twelfth. 10 twelfths make 10 ÷ 1 = 10 groups. So 56 ÷ 112 = 10. Check: 10 × 112 = 56.

items.e: Use fifths: 2 = 105. Each group is 2 fifths. 10 fifths make 10 ÷ 2 = 5 groups. So 2 ÷ 25 = 5. Check: 5 × 25 = 2.

items.q:
The bar shows 12. How many groups of 16 are in 12?
12 ÷ 16 = ?

items.q:
The bar shows 1 13. How many groups of 23 are in 1 13?
1 13 ÷ 23 = ?

items.q:
The bar shows 1. The pink part is not a full group. How many groups of 23 are in 1?
1 ÷ 23 = ?
items.e: Use thirds: 1 = 33. Each group is 2 thirds. 3 thirds make 1 full group, with 1 third left over. That 1 third is 12 of a group. So 1 ÷ 23 = 1 12. Check: 1 12 × 23 = 1.

items.q:
The bar shows 34. The pink part is not a full group. How many groups of 12 are in 34?
34 ÷ 12 = ?
items.e: Use fourths: 12 = 24. Each group is 2 fourths. 3 fourths make 1 full group, with 1 fourth left over. That 1 fourth is 12 of a group. So 34 ÷ 12 = 1 12. Check: 1 12 × 12 = 34.

items.q:
The bar shows 23. The pink part is not a full group. How many groups of 34 are in 23?
23 ÷ 34 = ?
items.e: Use twelfths: 23 = 812 and 34 = 912. Each group is 9 twelfths. There are only 8 twelfths, not enough for a full group. They make 89 of a group. So 23 ÷ 34 = 89. Check: 89 × 34 = 23.

56 ÷ 13 = ?
items.e: Use sixths: 13 = 26. Each group is 2 sixths. 5 sixths make 2 full groups, with 1 sixth left over. That 1 sixth is 12 of a group. So 56 ÷ 13 = 2 12. Check: 2 12 × 13 = 56.

items.e: Use sixths: 23 = 46. Each group is 1 sixth. 4 sixths make 4 ÷ 1 = 4 groups. So 23 ÷ 16 = 4. Check: 4 × 16 = 23.

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 35?
items.e: Flip it: the reciprocal is 53. Check: 35 × 53 = 1. The opposite −35 is a different idea.

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 4?
items.e: Write 4 as 41. Flip it: the reciprocal is 14. Check: 4 × 14 = 1.

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 17?
items.e: Flip it: the reciprocal is 7. Check: 17 × 7 = 1. (71 = 7.)

items.q: What is the reciprocal of 2 12?
items.e: Write 2 12 as 52. Flip it: the reciprocal is 25. Check: 52 × 25 = 1. Flipping only the 12 part (to get 2 + 2 = 4) is a common mistake.

items.q: 79 × ? = 1
items.e: A number times its reciprocal is 1. The reciprocal of 79 is 97: 79 × 97 = 6363 = 1. (29 is what you add to 79 to make 1, not what you multiply by.)

items.q: Which is the same as 56 ÷ 23?
c: 65 × 23
56 × 23
56 × 32
65 × 32
items.e: Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second number (the divisor). 56 ÷ 23 = 56 × 32 = 1 14.

items.q: Which is the same as 38 ÷ 14?
c: 38 × 14
83 × 14
items.e: Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second number (the divisor). 38 ÷ 14 = 38 × 4 = 1 12.

14 × 32

items.q: Which is the same as 34 ÷ 6?
c: 34 × 16
43 × 16
items.e: Keep the first number, change ÷ to ×, and flip only the second number (the divisor). 34 ÷ 6 = 34 × 16 = 18.

items.q: Which equation shows that 23 ÷ 34 = 89 is correct?
c: 23 × 34 = 89
34 × 89 = 23
23 × 89 = 34
89 ÷ 34 = 23
items.e: Division asks: what times 34 gives 23? 34 × 89 = 23, so 23 ÷ 34 = 89 is correct.

items.q: Which equation shows that 56 ÷ 13 = 2 12 is correct?
c: 13 × 2 12 = 56
2 12 ÷ 13 = 56
56 × 13 = 2 12

items.q: Which equation shows that 35 ÷ 910 = 23 is correct?
c: 35 × 910 = 23
910 × 23 = 35
35 × 23 = 910
23 ÷ 910 = 35
items.e: Division asks: what times 910 gives 35? 910 × 23 = 35, so 35 ÷ 910 = 23 is correct.

items.q: Which equation shows that 12 ÷ 38 = 1 13 is correct?
c: 12 × 1 13 = 38
1 13 ÷ 38 = 12
12 × 38 = 1 13
38 × 1 13 = 12
items.e: Division asks: what times 38 gives 12? 38 × 1 13 = 12, so 12 ÷ 38 = 1 13 is correct.

items.q: Without computing, 56 ÷ 13 is ___.
items.e: You divide by a number less than 1, so the quotient is greater than 56 (it is 2 12).

items.q: Without computing, 34 ÷ 1 12 is ___.
items.e: You divide by a number greater than 1, so the quotient is less than 34 (it is 12).

items.q: Without computing, 25 ÷ 45 is ___.
items.e: You divide by a number less than 1, so the quotient is greater than 25 (it is 12).

items.q: Which quotient is greater than 1?
c: 13 ÷ 34
25 ÷ 12
35 ÷ 12
12 ÷ 35
items.e: A quotient is greater than 1 when the first number is greater than the second. 35 is greater than 12, so 35 ÷ 12 = 1 15. The others are less than 1.

items.q: Which quotient is less than 1?
c: 78 ÷ 38
56 ÷ 23
23 ÷ 56
34 ÷ 12
items.e: A quotient is less than 1 when the first number is less than the second. 23 is less than 56, so 23 ÷ 56 = 45. The others are greater than 1.

items.q: 3 friends share 12 pound of chocolate equally. How much chocolate does each friend get?
items.e: Split 12 pound into 3 equal parts: 12 ÷ 3 = 12 × 13 = 16 pound. Check: 16 × 3 = 12.

items.q: One serving of yogurt is 34 cup. How many servings are in 23 cup of yogurt?
c: 12 of a serving
89 of a serving
items.e: Find how many 34-cup servings fit in 23 cup: 23 ÷ 34 = 23 × 43 = 89 of a serving. Check: 89 × 34 = 23. There is not enough for 1 full serving, so the answer is less than 1.

items.q: A rectangular strip of land is 34 mile long. Its area is 12 square mile. How wide is it?
items.e: Area = length × width, so width = area ÷ length: 12 ÷ 34 = 12 × 43 = 23 mile. Check: 23 × 34 = 12.

items.q: A rectangular garden is 2 12 yards long. Its area is 3 34 square yards. How wide is it?
items.e: Width = area ÷ length: 3 34 ÷ 2 12 = 154 × 25 = 1 12 yards. Check: 1 12 × 2 12 = 3 34.

items.q: Leo has 5 14 yards of ribbon. He cuts it into pieces that are each 34 yard long. How many pieces does he get?
items.e: Find how many 34-yard pieces are in 5 14 yards: 5 14 ÷ 34 = 214 × 43 = 7 pieces. Check: 7 × 34 = 5 14.

items.e: Find how many 13-pound bags are in 2 23 pounds: 2 23 ÷ 13 = 83 × 3 = 8 bags. Check: 8 × 13 = 2 23.

items.e: Find how many 34-cup amounts are in 6 cups: 6 ÷ 34 = 6 × 43 = 8 batches. Check: 8 × 34 = 6.

c: 316 mile per hour
13 mile per hour
items.e: Divide the distance by the time: 34 ÷ 14 = 34 × 4 = 3 miles per hour. Check: 3 × 14 = 34.

items.e: Find how many 1 14-foot shelves are in 7 12 feet: 7 12 ÷ 1 14 = 152 × 45 = 6 shelves. Check: 6 × 1 14 = 7 12.

items.e: Find how many 56-hour quizzes fit in 2 12 hours: 2 12 ÷ 56 = 52 × 65 = 3 quizzes. Check: 3 × 56 = 2 12.

items.q: A cook has 5 pounds of rice. Each portion uses 23 pound. How many full portions can the cook make?
items.e: 5 ÷ 23 = 5 × 32 = 152 = 7 12 portions. Only whole portions count, so the cook can make 7 full portions (with 13 pound left over).

items.q: Nora has 4 cups of soup. Each bowl holds 23 cup. Which expression shows how many bowls she can fill?
items.e: The question asks how many 23-cup bowls fit in 4 cups, so divide 4 by 23: 4 ÷ 23 = 4 × 32 = 6 bowls. Check: 6 × 23 = 4.

items.q: Which question can you answer with 34 ÷ 18?
c: How many 34-cup scoops are in 18 cup?
How many 18-cup scoops are in 34 cup?
What is 18 of 34 cup?

items.e: 34 ÷ 18 asks how many eighths are in 34: 34 = 68, so 6 scoops. “18 of 34” is multiplication, and the reversed question is 18 ÷ 34.

items.q: Mia pours 2 cups of milk into 13-cup glasses. Grace pours 2 12 cups of milk into 12-cup glasses. Who fills more glasses?
items.e: Mia: 2 ÷ 13 = 6 glasses. Grace: 2 12 ÷ 12 = 52 × 2 = 5 glasses. 6 is more than 5, so Mia fills more glasses. She has less milk, but 13-cup glasses are smaller.
